themes.label: Paywall locks core study features
themes.summary: Users across Android and iOS say Quizlet used to be a free study tool and that the Learn mode, practice tests, and flashcard limits now require a Quizlet+ subscription after a limited number of rounds. Many are students or low-income users who say the roughly $45 to $48 annual price, or monthly fees, put the core study function out of reach, and some report the free tier feels too restrictive to be useful. A few also mention the subscription being hard to cancel and recurring app prompts to subscribe.
themes.recommendation: Analyze conversion and churn by app version (v6.23 through v10.5) and by region to identify when the free-tier limits were introduced, then test a student-priced plan or a rewarded-ad option for extra Learn and Test rounds to see if it reduces 1-star reviews without cutting subscription revenue.

themes.label: Paywall blocks core study modes
themes.summary: Many reviewers praise Quizlet's flashcard creation and shared sets but say that learn and writing modes, sorting, and downloads moved behind Quizlet Plus, often without warning. Several long-time users feel the free tier is now too limited for studying, and a few mention bugs when editing cards on mobile, such as lost pictures or unsaved terms.
themes.recommendation: Audit which study modes and features moved behind the paywall since v7, then pull paywall and upgrade-prompt analytics on free-user learn and writing sessions to decide whether any core modes should return to the free tier or be clearly labelled before a user builds a set.

themes.label: Post-update AI and paywall complaints
themes.summary: Users in this cluster say the app got worse after updates, especially when AI features and a stricter paywall were introduced, with some saying AI answers are often wrong and that core study features now require payment. Complaints span both iOS and Android across several versions from 2022 to 2026, and some reviewers note that answer checking became too lenient or that the app now makes decisions for them. Mixed in are short five-star praise comments, but the dominant theme is dissatisfaction with changes to the product.
themes.recommendation: Pull the release notes and crash/accuracy data for v10.47 and the recent AI-feature rollouts, then investigate the answer-checking regression (e.g., near-match spelling accepted as correct) and add a rollback or opt-out toggle for AI-generated content in settings.

themes.label: Praise: study app effectiveness
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are overwhelmingly praising Quizlet as an effective, easy, and fun way to study, with many saying it helped them memorize vocabulary and pass tests. Several mention specific features they value, including flashcards, practice quizzes, learn mode, and the newer AI tool that generates flashcards and study guides from pasted text or scanned files. A minority of reviews mention friction, mainly that free users hit limits on tests or learn mode, offline access is paywalled, and some feel the free tier has shrunk.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core study loop (flashcards, learn mode, and practice tests) in any monetization changes, and A/B test whether the AI flashcard generator can be showcased to free users as a conversion path to Plus.

themes.label: Praise: study tool helpfulness
themes.summary: Users across iOS and Android say Quizlet helps them memorize material, prepare for tests, and study more efficiently, with frequent mentions of flashcards, the learn mode, and progress tracking. A minority of reviews mention paywall frustration around the free tier's study limits and a few report occasional bugs such as crashes or incorrect quiz spelling.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core learn and flashcard experience in the free tier while reviewing the free-versus-paid boundary, and pull crash and incorrect-spelling reports from the last two app versions into a triage ticket to check whether they cluster on a specific platform or release.

themes.label: Free tier paywall restrictions
themes.summary: Many reviewers praise Quizlet as a useful study tool, but a large share of the cluster complains that free features such as Learn, Test, practice rounds, offline flashcard access and image uploads have moved behind Quizlet Plus or trial limits. Several long-time users say the app now feels focused on subscriptions, and some note that AI tools are also gated, with alternatives like Anki or AI flashcard apps mentioned as replacements.
themes.recommendation: Audit the free-tier limits by feature (Learn, Test, offline flashcards, image upload, AI tools) and compare them against the release notes for v8 through v10, then test whether restoring one or two of the most cited free features, such as offline flashcard access, reduces 1 to 2 star reviews and free-to-paid churn in an A/B test.

themes.label: Praise: study helpfulness
themes.summary: Users in this cluster are mostly short, generic praise, calling Quizlet good, helpful, cool, or useful for tests and learning, with almost no specific feature requests. A few mention studying math or quizzes and one notes the app shuts down mid-test, though that complaint is buried in otherwise positive text.
themes.recommendation: Protect the core study experience and pull the few mentions of the app shutting down during tests into a crash investigation, reviewing iOS crash logs for sessions that run long or are active during a quiz.

themes.label: Paywall limits free study features
themes.summary: Most reviews in this cluster praise Quizlet for helping students study and prepare for exams, but a recurring group says that core features are locked behind a roughly $50/year subscription. Users point to limits such as one test per list, no way to save lists, and the scan feature being paid even during the free trial, and some say this is hard on students who can't afford it. A few reviewers also mention the app feeling dated or crashing on newer iPhones.
themes.recommendation: Audit the free-tier versus paid-tier feature gates (single test per list, list saving, scan during trial) and test whether relaxing one or two of them, or clarifying trial limits before purchase in the French locale, reduces paywall complaints without hurting conversion.

reviews.t: Not as good as it used to be
reviews.x: I’ve been using Quizlet since high school (when the app was free) and over the years I’ve noticed how worse the app has gotten. I cancelled my subscription because why am I paying $44.99/year for an app that doesn’t even work. 1) The ‘Still Practicing’ option for terms and definitions I haven’t mastered yet will give me the same ones I’ve gotten wrong in the previous ‘Not Practiced’ option in Learn. Why do I have to restart learn or take a test to keep practicing? Why can’t I go through all of my questions until they’re in mastered BEFORE I take a test? 2) I think there should be more than three other possible answers for a question on the multiple choice option. I don’t understand why it isn’t more than three other possible choices because it’s a feature that comes with premium. 3) I miss being able to copy and paste my notes into Quizlet WITHOUT the app immediately taking me to the website. I don’t understand why that has to happen because before I would be able to copy and paste my notes and I was able to generate a study guide STRICTLY based on my notes and not bad AI-generated data collected from resources that are vaguely related to the topic, not specific or a lot of the times just straight up misinformation. I also don’t like that it separates notes into multiple categories, when before the app would collect all your notes and make a study guide/flashcards with everything from my uploaded notes in one study set. Is there a way to turn off the magic notes feature and just make it regular notes? Quizlet Premium is not worth your money in my opinion because there are cheaper options that provide extra attributes that are also neurodivergent friendly (ie. half-bold text and Audiobook generators). Invest your money on Mindgrasp or Study Fetch!!!!

reviews.t: do not download, unless you want to spend money
reviews.x: I want to make it clear that I'm not leaving a 1 star review because there's a paid tier, and not even because most of the content is paid. I don't think there's anything wrong with offering a paid service. The problem is that this app used to be an amazing free resource for students. They had a paid upgrade with perks, you could support them if you had the money, but you could still use the app and get a lot of good from it without paying. Most students live on a tight budget, so it really was something essential that they could depend on. Now you can't do anything if you don't pay a yearly subscription. You'll actually learn nothing, and you won't be able to study with this app if you don't give them money. They give you a ridiculously small limited amount of practice per set of flashcards. This company made the decision to remove a free resource for students. They know that students spent hours putting their learning materials on their website, and that they often have busy schedules so they'll feel compelled to spend money on a paid subscription to have access to it. It's quite a disgusting practice in my opinion and I would never support a company like this.

I would use the “learn” mode throughout the semester, then do the flash card mode in preparation for exams. That served me very well and it helped me earn very high marks. I am now going back to school and am dismayed to find out that Quizlet has introduced a 5 round limit to the learn mode, otherwise you have to pay to use it. I could understand making some of the fancier features pay to use, but making the most basic and important feature the one that you have to pay for? That’s ridiculous. I will be finding an alternative app.

reviews.t: Amazing app for learning and studying

As an added bonus, not much is locked behind Quizlet Plus, making it much easier to get everything done. Creating study sets is also very easy. Would highly recommend to anyone in grade school to high school.

While the app is very helpful, being able to adjust the text placement and size of the text within the app would make it much more user friendly. Not everyone can see the text at the current size. I am using it to learn Thai and it is important to see enough detail to know which letter is which, but that's very hard to do as the app stands now. I would like to increase the text size and be able to choose the text to be centered whenever displayed to maximize use of the screen and legibility.

I think this app is very good especially for subjects where you have to memorize a lot of concepts. This app is especially useful for Anatomy, because Anatomy is full of difficult concepts, and there is plenty of information to memorize. I think Quizlet can also help with making good flashcards for anatomy to help with studying. Overall, it's a ln excellent app for Anatomy students as well as people in other difficult subjects. I would highly recommend this app to anybody!

Quizlet is enjoyable to use. It let's you choose what type of studying you are in the mood for, whether it is flashcards, a matching game, or it gets tougher by typing your answers. I've been playing for free for about a week now, but will be signing up soon. I figure if quizlet has kept me engaged and excited then it's definitely worth the small price for the year. Try it, it's awesome!

I learned how to actually study with flashcards from the app. It's helpful and even has extra exercises to encourage you to learn. There are modes of learning for all learners, visual, auditory, and tactile (you can type the answers, I personally found that option super helpful). Using it on both the computer and the app is great too. The computer lets you easily upload your terms and definitions in one go, and also provides some different activities and games to practice with. Super helpful.

Quizlet is a great study tool have used them sic e I discovered it in my freshman year of college. I would suggest a few improvements like being able to combine some study sets in a random selection and order and an intentional selection and order. Not really necessary but I think being able to color code items would be helpful and a great way to make the site/app more personal.

Used Quizlet for years. It was a main tool for me. However, the Plus version is way too pricey for students now. Additionally the Learn Mode has been changed for the worse. It is way too easy. Before, words that you got wrong had to be repeated twice before you "mastered" them. Now you "master" them WAY too easily. Also cards would show up as MCQ first, then from 1 side, and finally from the other side. You should make the Old Learn an option - perhaps Hard Mode? Happy to buy it again once fixed

I LOVE this app! I am paying for QuizletPlus.I am learning Arabic and it is such a difficult language. This app allows me to set up my vocab lists in a way that suits me. I can add clues (within brackets), I can put in my own images to give myself a hint. I can look for the vocab lists set up by other people (e.g. for my textbook, Al Kitaab) and then copy their list and tweak it for my own needs. The Learning system is really good and I have made huge progress in my Arabic over the last year. I love the starring facility to mark particular words in the list. So for example, if you find a particular set of words difficult, you can star them and review only those words. (NB to Quizlet, I would love to have a couple more star colours so that I can reorganise my list in different ways.) I thoroughly recommend to anyone studying a language.

It used to be great. And then they launched a new version of the Learn mode which deleted the progresses on current deck. The new version forces to see a bunch of new terms before moving to written question, it's not very efficient... Sad.. The app is still a good tool. Just disappointed with this new version..

I use this app to study Japanese vocabulary. It's not simply a flashcards' app, there are a lot of different activities such as match, write, learn etc. You also have the option to combine multiple decks in one study session without needing to actually merge the sets! I really recommend it. I don't have the paid version, but even the free version is totally worth it!

On iOS, there's an option to study an entire folder, allowing me to study all vocab at once. That option is not available on this app, so now I have to finish one set at a time then exit all the way out to main screen, then pick the next folder. I just can't wrap my head around why it isnt here but elsewhere. PLEASE FIX

For example, I made study sets for my 3 chapters in my science book and I made folders named science chapter 1, science chapter 2 etc... but then it's all cluttered because I also do the same with my other subjects. How about you add a feature where we could put a folder inside a folder? This could really help.

I really enjoy the app and its functions! I've been using it almost 4 years now 👍 Please, add notifications for active recall (the forgetting curve) in order to send the words to the long memory. And it would be great if you had a function for teachers to see how their students are dealing with the sets. I have to search other apps for this, but if you had these functions, that would be really helpful 🙏

This app is fantastic if all you're looking for is flashcards. I used it to get great scores in a few of my early medical classes. However, in order to continue to be useful the app would really need the spaced repetition features other apps have. As I go through school I'm starting to need to memorize larger amounts of information, and spaced repetition helps me focus on what I don't know instead of having to go through entire decks. If you don't need that though, this app is fantastic!

If I could give a zero star review I would. I love everything about quizlet EXCEPT that now working off of wifi (even with data) requires a paid subscription. Change this. There is no reason that for me to study offline I should have to pay. I don't mind paying for other cool features and such, but that gives me no reason to use Quizlet paper flash cards instead.

I would love to give the app 5 stars. Unfortunately, I constantly keep receiving a "no internet connection " message. Once I see that I'm unable to access the study sets I have saved. It then refers me to purchasing quizlet plus. That alone makes using the app quite frustrating. I definitely need access to the sets I have saved , its vital for the courses I am taking. I wish the developers would do better with this.

For native English speakers, Japanese is an incredibly hard language to learn. Quizlet makes it a hell of a lot easier. I use it in combination with NihonGO NOW. As someone who's taken Japanese before the smart app was invented I can tell you that it's a lot easier learning the language with the convenience and availability to study anywhere. Your need to study anything that is even remotely difficult, pay the extra for the plus. It's worth it.

This app was extremely helpful to me as I am always on the go and constantly would forget my physical flash cards. Besides just being a mobile, take anywhere, easy access flashcard app, it has many different ways to help you study. I really liked the matching game and the ability to have it read the cards to me and I'd say it as I listened to the app read it and I read them at the same time! It's super convenient and super user friendly! You can organize your cards and even search.

This app is awesome. I'm able to take all my key terms from any given study chapter, create a study set, and go over them any time, even on the go. I also appreciate the practice tests. It helps me determine which concepts I'm getting and which I need to focus more intensely on. I like the folders option as well, I use them to group study sets for chapters that will be the focus of my next exam.

It's a great app, quite easy to use. The free version is very functional too. Note: If the app doesn't give auto suggestion while typing a new word or word definition, switch network to mobile data. On my device, the app gives the error message "No internet connection" when connected to my WiFi. This happened after the most recent update. Now I use it only on mobile data and it works perfectly.

Everything's working well except that I don't like the design of the flashcards. I prefer the simples one like the one in the desktop version. I can't slide to the previous card either. I hope you can also add a search box within the set so we don't have to scroll through a thousand terms to look for it.

First, it's very easy to use, beginner friendly. Second, it's very cute! I mean, white is one of the most used and most common color out there but the design of this app is so cute! Third, you can make a LOT of flashcards and they have lots of options to learn. You can also choose the "test" type and when you do it, it's like you're taking an exam! This really helps for my exams and that's why I'm posting a review right now. Because it really helps. Thanks for making this app! ✨ It's freee!!! ✨

It's really great for studying flash card material and sharing with other classmates. I have paid for the GO level, but it doesn't seems to work well offline for the sets I have downloaded to my device. The app always just spins when I don't have WiFi (I don't have a data plan on my phone). I was hoping with the GO level my kids could use the app on a tablet in the car, but it doesn't work.

I didn't have the "plus" option for a long time. I have since upgraded and love it. I am using it for medical terminology right now and love the option to take a picture of my notes to create flashcards (by highlighting the words in my notes). I also like that I can add pictures to study some of the visual/ anatomy things I need to know. Plus having the app on my phone, I am able to study anywhere. Which means extra study time.

I spent 3 hours making over 100 flash cards that ended up erasing themselves after I checked back. I thought I wouldn’t have to worry about my work disappearing but boy was I wrong. Sucks that I have a test tomorrow and I relied on this to help me review my notes. Should’ve just did them on microsoft word...

I was confused at first, I usually use quizlet online. I thought that you had to pay for learning mode. I was upset, I downloaded the app and you didn't need to pay for it, it's free. You can pay for it if you want your custom study path. Also upset that when doing the learning mode, I think there should be a FREE option to put images for terms as well, or it can get confusing. That's all! The learning mode is the part that gets me excited the most to study! Having quizlet for 2 years! :)

It's super for all sorts of study material. I even use it for Psychology Class! (Edit Sep 2020): used the PLUS service for years, at $20 bucks a year, couldn't pass it up -auto renewed! I just noticed the price had MORE than DOUBLED at &50! Minus one Star, still a great service, no longer as affordable. Why such a ridiculously steep increase in price? Some minor, unspectacular changes. It was probably worth it to begin with, just harder for a poor student to afford - I can pass it up now!

Great but I have some suggestions. On mobile, the images on flashcards are large and sometimes make the text too small to read comfortably, it would be nice to have the option to toggle images on mobile. Also, the option to hide flashcards in sets (without deleting them) would also be a nice feature. Lastly, Please let us sort folders by alphabetical order I'm the app. Thanks for providing a convenient study service!

This app is great! I just hope you can add an option of studying the folder itself so that we can study all the sets in a folder altogether and in shuffle. On the other hand, I'm having a hard time finding a term I wish to delete especially when there are many terms in a set. Maybe you can put numbers beside the terms when they are sorted "originally" and when we are on the "edit set" section, or make an option wherein we can view the "edit set" section alphabetically.

Literally the best. If you're looking for an app that guides you through your revising process,you have come to the right place! Quizlet is an absolute life saver for any school or learning material you have to encounter. You can create your very own flashcards either on notes, concepts or key terms ,actually anything really :) This app is nothing but the best of all time. I love that you can look up a certain topic and packs that were created by others. I would love if gravity mode was mobile!

Very helpful to use the flashcards. Having access to other people's sets is extremely time saving. Would've been rated 5 stars if creating new flashcards was more user friendly. Need more options for typing words like italics and bold. Being able to change the color of words would be bonus. Otherwise, I do recommend getting this app.

Downloaded this a year ago and it was absolutely great! It really helped me in reviewing for my past examinations. Though, in my experience with the app, I think it would be better if one is able to access the quizzes without internet connection for free. Most students who doesn't earn money yet would find that really really helpful.

This app is great, just read all the other comments. BUT I'd like to propose a new option: I think it would be interesting to be able to also have "long-term lists", I mean lists we wanna master forever, not just for a test or whatever. For that, I think it would be a good option to have a way to interrogate on the words in function of what we did since the beginning of our learning of the list. A way to interrogate on a list that will never be considered as totally mastered.

My favorite app! Thanks to everyone those who's been working on Quizlet. I can't think of an app which would suit me better in memorizing those never-ending lists of vocabulary and other things which have to memorize for uni. Quizlet has also broadened my horizons as far as general geography and biology are concerned (the countries of Africa, the parts of a flower...). It's also very convenient to paste there entire lists of vocabulary (e.g., from Word) and start learning straight away.

Progress doesn't update when learning a set, and gets stuck on 3%. Can't delete, merge or duplicate sets. On the website it says there are options for Long Term Learning (like spaced repetition), but there's only one way to get through the Learn mode. There should be a way to study a set (and revising it after adding a few words) that's proportional to the last time you've repeated certain terms!

I've dabbled with flashcard apps a few times, and I always get to the initial stages and get stumped or irritated or run out of time or energy to find out how to do things. This one is perfect, I got in and immediately made a deck to suit me plus found another someone else had made that I liked, it was fast and intuitive and so much better than the others I've tried, and this week I've learn new vocab so much more easily! Very pleased. Recommend.

This app is really useful and my choice out of many. It has quite a large library of user-made cards you can study from or choose to create your very own flashcard set. It's also comes with reading the flashcards for you, perfect for learning a second language. My only issue is that it's really hard to edit or add new your flashcard as you will need to scroll through your full list of cards, would have been great if adding can be from the top and editing can be done easier.

This is a great tool for fun learning. My grades have increased because of this app. Including me, needing extra practice in their studies, and retaining information seemed impossible before I come to use this app. No more spending time writing on flash cards, especially for those who has bad handwriting. This is eco friendly, and convenient for students. Very user-friendly.

This app has helped EMMENSLEY in getting me through college. I am a free version user. I have two problems with this app, and I hope the developers read this: 1. I think the notecards should be numbered individually to help keep track of which ones are studied, and to know how far you've gotten. It also would help with remembering them 2. I really wish I could edit the notecards as I'm studying them. I lost count of the amount of times I have seen a spelling error.

Amazing app!!! Really helpful for language learners. I used the free version, beside not being able to put pictures into flashcards, everything else is great. I got most benefits I can expect from the free version. I do expect that when i create many sets and put them into 1 folder, i can study the whole folder altogethe. I made sets to keep track on my study, but i do wish to study the whole folder to have a general view of my progress. If you can add that, it would be great 😍 thank you

5 stars because its the best and cheapest one I've used so far. 1. There is a free option: Use it online and access it on your computer or on your phone. Allows you to use basic flashcards (typing on both sides) and you can access other peoples sets. Thats all I really needed it for but I went ahead and bought the $20 a year thing. Can make your own flash cards with photos which I need to expand and improve my learning. Im studying anatomy and shadowing 2 PT, NDs so it really helps.

This app is the ultimate study guide. You can create multiple sets of cards. If a particular card stumps you every time you see it, click the star. You have the option later to study only the starred ones so you can concentrate on the things you need help with the most! Also, you can see similar questions & answers to what you're typing, allowing you to select those and save time. One suggestion would be to make finding & editing particular cards easier, instead of having to hunt thru the set.

I needed something to be able to practice for my CompTIA exam. Some of the terms I needed to remember were number based and I'm lousy with remembering numbers. I was able to setup a list with 20 protocols and their port numbers and the app just setup a randomized multiple choice test that I could do over and over again until I was answering every question correctly. I would have used this months ago if I knew about it. The best part is it has a website that you can log into, create lists from there instead of your cell phone, and it can be accessible from any portable device that has access to the app.

5/5 ☆'s I have the plus version for my studies and absolutely love the features, so far they've been beyond helpful especially since I cant really study with a laptop/computer out (children and pet distractions). Also I have the availability to keep my studies private, merge different studies, be at my own pace, and the offline feature is awesome for me as I've been traveling a bunch lately.

I tried both Anki and Quizlet, they are both great. Anki has lot of features and customization items, and free. But I chose Quizlet in the end and purchase pro version, because it is easy to set up a set of cards. It is compatible with Windows, so I can use my work computer to log in quizlet website and set a deck to learn at my break time and sync with my phone. Quizlet has more testing features make learning like playing games. If quizlet can show IPA, then it is perfect for me.

Needs improvement. Agree with the other comments. There needs to be a merge/split set option. Also, I like the scan document icon but only available when you first create the set then it disappears after you saved the set. Also, you can't delete the set from the folder on the app; and you can't shift the order of the cards by dragging it, it can only be done on the computer version but not the app.. Please also have an option to display which sets to display on the main page

I didn't know that flashcard apps were that advanced nowadays. I got the "go" premium membership to remove the ads, that's fair. Only complaint : The auto completion when creating sets is great, but the way it's made doesn't make much sense to me. I'm learning Russian vocabulary and the app picked that up very well, but as soon as I've written a Russian word it should suggest the English translation as a "definition" instead of suggesting the word I just typed.

I used this a few years ago and wasn't very impressed, but it's improved dramatically. AnkiApp was always my flashcard app of choice, but this has now surpassed it. With a greater range of games/puzzles it makes the flashcard experience more fun and consequently easier to keep up. The only thing I find annoying (but not enough to lose a star) is the smug "Welcome back, it's been a while" message, especially as I use the app daily. Overall though it's a great addition to language learning.

Won't let me study and demands I pay for offline mode when I'm online! :( Every other app works fine on the Internet. Just this one has problems and says that I have to pay to study. What a waste of time making those study sets and I can't use them as the option is greyed out. I've also had to go through the pain on the occasion the app does work... Which is rare, I can't edit or create new sets as it doesn't recognise me wanting to select the card to type in. I have to close and reopen the app

Quick and simple. A variety of ways to study your flash cards, although I mostly use the simple "flashcard" and "write" options. When specifying the language you are studying, Quizlet gives suggestions for translations, making everything quicker. One can also add pictures (maybe only free on desktop), and there is a really nice, really dark dark-mode.

If I could give zero stars I would. I like the app for studying for sure, but I trialed the premium, haven't used it more than once and am unable to cancel. I've tried several times to no avail, so of course I was charged $28 whatever for the year. Save yourself the $ & don't upgrade. You won't be able to get out of it!! Every time I try the help center I get a page that says it doesn't exist.

Easy to use. I like the different learning formats - flash cards, matching, practice tests. My main criticism is the terms look to be written by laypeople, maybe even non-English speakers. The definitions are simplistic and somewhat nonstandard. Also, the system that checks the accuracy of your answer is annoying. You could answer correctly but fail to match the exact wording the app wants or even forget to add an S to pluralize a word, and it marks you wrong. Good study supplement only.

I wanted to give it a higher rating because I really enjoy this app BUT I have a major gripe. I use quizlet for Japanese, and when I use the 'learn' mode, it goes through the 'terms' in junks. However, if you get stuck on a few terms and don't master them, it puts them at bottom of your familiar terms and makes you start learning the next set and you learn the previous terms until mastering the terms built up on top of the previous familiar terms. This just makes it harder to study and review.

The Quizlet plus is incredible. But I would prefer to see a language selection option customized on each card. On the current version, once you change a language on one card, the change becomes global. For instance, sometimes it is more convenient to see a definition of a term in English, and at other times you may prefer to listen to the meaning in German for the sake of reminding yourself of the pronunciation. If definitions are in more than one language, pronunciation becomes unintelligible.

An useful app that everyone who's studying should try. It's perfect for memorizing: there's a range of different little "games" which through short tasks make your learning process fun and different from usual. From flashcards to simple writing, you can find the ones you are more comfortable with, edit or search them and then study! You can also receive notifications that will remind you to study before your exam/test.

Love this app, but I can't use night theme on my phone, all my definition do not appear on my card like if I'm listing functions, it doesn't even show 😔 Update 1/2/20: I can now use my night time theme on my phone and not just my laptop. I love this app. I wish they could give the option to go back to the previous flash card to review not just when it's wrong. I like to reread.

I wish that when i set several (many) flashcard sets for a certain "test date" using settings for the "learn" function, the app would be able to adapt my studies accordingly based on not only the last time i quizzed myself using "learn" but also how badly i need to study that set. As of now, say if I set 10 sets to be tested in 1 month, for the next month I'll get 10 reminders (1/set) every day to practice the sets whether i have mastered them or not, rather than spaced out according to need.

Amaaazing! Been using this to study Japanese Kanji for a few years now and it's always helped me with a fast study for exams in University haha. Now I use it to review vocabulary I'm starting to forget, will always love it. The best part about it is that you can put everything in an Excel file and then just copy & paste everything at once to create your flashcards, no need to make them one at a time. 5 stars, keep it up

The functionality, especially trying to combine terms into a folder or a single class is arduous. Yea, it's free but I just can not see myself wanting to pay when it has the prior issues plus uploading window docs in plain text gets fumbled by this app, too. I do recommend for a very basic basic use (same as making/writing your own flashcards).

I love Quizlet. It has helped me ace my memorization heavy nursing classes. I would pay way more than the $20 yearly for this program. I love the "learn" function, because I am able to keep track of what I have mastered so that I don't waste time studying things I already know. I also love that I can add pictures to the flash cards, as it helps with memorization and recall. Quizlet streamlines my study process.

I am a college student and this is my go to app for studying. I have sets for all my classes and I even helped my lab partner by just giving her my username to search so she could study using my sets. It's really cool how there are a lot of different ways to study your sets and test yourself. Match, multiple choice, typed answer, plain old flipping etc. Only little problem is if you want to edit a set that has rich format text you have to do it on the website; at least on my device.

Very helpful - THANK YOU for making it work offline that saved me! I also love the simplicity in using it and finding other decks :) I don't think I'll use the quiz options ( got to use them, love them) Question/Sugesstion: can I merge different study sets into one? It would be really useful because I study by chapter and then mixing all the facts from one level into one would really help with the final review.

One of the best apps for flashcards. I'm studying for an exam and Quizlet is making my study time a breeze! It's not just flash cards. It turns your 'cards' into an interactive game. And gives you many ways that you can study the information and I find that this combination helps me retain the information better.

Making sets of flashcards and sharing them with classmates (or anyone on Earth with the app and your permission) exemplifies tech eliminating redundancy . A list can be divided by many students and all of the list "pieces" can then be shared together. This is very efficient because you could produce a relevant set of reviewable flashcard vocabulary in a class with very little effort. The structure and layout of cards is limited by design, but can still be highly customized within that system.

PART 3: I'm not finding this app very helpful. They're just don't seem to be enough resources. Plus, I don't want to choose a set that has 400 words! I'm having a hell of a time canceling out my subscription. It's like an endless mass of hurdles! PART 2: Looks like this is part 2. The only huge problem I found with this site is that there are not enough resources in the language in which I'm studying. I'm having a heck of a time canceling out my subscription.

Quizlet is very useful, it allows me to effectively learn information and lets me set when my study date is and reminds me to look at my study set(s) again. Even if you don't want to make your own, you can also use other people's. There is always some on what you need to revise. Overall Quizlet has helped me a lot and I've never experienced any problems. Hope this helps!

I love using this for studying and testing yourself. You can also let it know that a test is coming up so it will send you reminders daily to study, it is a good motivator. I mainly use the premade desks, if you have a popular textbook they are easy to find. Although you can make your own and customize pictures making it easier for you to remember.

I love this app! I normally have a very hard time learning vocabulary but with quizlet its a lot easier. I bought the one year subscription for 20 dollars and I am very happy I did. I can take a picture of my terms and scan them into the app. I can make flashcards for several chapters very quickly which allows me to have more time to actually focus on studying them. I've been getting 80s on my quizzes now. thank you quizlet!❤

So theoretically, Quizlet itself is a great study tool. Having it on my phone is great, and it's easily worth the money. However as an app, I cannot believe that I'm paying for something that runs soooo slow. I cannot navigate this app at this speed. Sometimes i have to wait over a minute to go from one page to another, and up to 5 minutes for a study set to load so i can even see what's in it. The concept is worth the money. The functionality is not.

It's pretty helpful for learning and memorizing material for tests. The app filters out the questions you have struggled with and focuses more on those. There is also a wide variety of material on almost any subject. The only issue I had was some answers were spelled incorrectly and when doing practice tests , I would get it wrong unless I copied their incorrect spelling. This was only the case in a couple of questions. Overall the app is very helpful.

It was a good app. I wanted to take up a monthly subscription. But before that even happened it automatically deducted amount from my account without even notifying me. That to a yearly subscription. It's not even been a month with the trail. I could not even find a way to disable the subscription in the app nor the help centre. I guess the user should accept the way as it so complicated. Kindly cancel my subscription and refund my amount. Very dissatisfied.

This new update it’s screwing everything up? I hate how the entire page gets filled up to put your definitions/terms. And on top of that sometimes the terms appear in the definitions and the definitions appear in the terms ?????? What the actual heck man?????? FIX ASAP i have 2 midterms I’m prepping for for next week, i need this fixed. I’m so stressed, and this app screwing up is the last thing i need rn

I never thought that I would be able to learn this fast, what I like even more is the difference options to learn and practice, be it flashcards of writing, etc. Really recommend it. The only issue that I've found was that it doesn't always read the words out loud or just doesn't it whenever it wants and that's not really helpful,hope u fix that!

I love the website but the app is lacking. You can't edit flashcards in your sets, and when you go into study mode only the first line on the back of the card shows (its missing almost all information on the back of the flashcard). In study mode the cards can't rotate horizontally either. If these point can be improved upon I will definitly raise my rating. I understand that app might not be be able to support the editing, but the other issues definitely need to be fixed.

On a desktop, Quizlet added functionality to easily bold, italicize, and even highlight info on the flashcard which is great. However, when viewing cards on a mobile device that contain words that are both bold and non-bold, or words that are underlined and non-underlined on one slide, it doesn't display all of the words! They're simply just not there. I thought I forgot to add the info when I created the set on a computer, but they appear correctly on a desktop. Are you kidding me?!

reviews.t: EVERY TIME I MAKE A NEW FLASH CARD THE CONTENTS OF THE PREVIOUS ONE DELETES
reviews.x: THERES A GLITCH OR SOMETHING AND EVERY TIME I MAKE A NEW CARD BY CLICKING TAB, THE PREVIOUS CARD’S CONTENTS ERASES? ALSO SOMETIMES WHEN I LEAVE A SET AND COME BACK SOME OF MY CARDS ARE MISSING CONTENT. PLS FIX I HIGHLY DEPEND ON THIS APP FOR STUDYING

This is a great app. By far one of the best study tools around. I'm currently using it for anatomy, and it's making everything so much easier to learn. I love the way it figures out your weak points and grills you on them until you master all of your cards. For anything you need to memorize (especially diagrams), this app is your best bet.

LOVE THIS RESOURCE! Only one suggestion, when entering the data in a study set on the desktop, the intuitive suggestion (AWESOME btw), does not make the suggestion selectable WITHOUT mouse. Anyone familiar with other software's use tab, arrow, enter from the keyboard, but in Quizlet you have to leave the keyboard to select with mouse!?! At that point it's just as fast to type it myself! Just saying!

As a pre-med major this app has honeslty saved my life on multiple occasions. It is so much more convenient to have digital flashcards that you can access & easily search through at all times. Quizlet even lets you not only star what you need to work on but also has the option to "swipe left or right" if you've learned the flashcard. I tried Anki for a while but in my opinion, Quizlet is the best by far!

Great overall but with several areas needing improvement. One in particular; it would be nice to be able to copy and paste an existing flash card in one set, over to another set. For instance, if I'm studying a language and categorizing vocabulary words, I might decide I've got a group of words that could be their own study set or I need extra focus on them. Right now I would have to recreate all those flash cards in the new set. If I could copy and paste, it would save valuable study time.

I installed it for college and I'm loving it so far. I can review my study sets whenever and wherever with this convenient app. :) But on another note, I agree with other users that there should be sound effects for choosing the right or wrong answers. Also, for tests, I recommend letting the right answer stay on screen for longer especially if I got it wrong.

This app lets you drag and drop lists of material to memorize and generates the flashcards for you! I take my teachers' handouts and then make my flashcards in just seconds! Then the app even makes games too! You can study by flipping the cards, then play matching, then write in answers (and more). Also, then all my cards are simply in my phone. Stuck in line at the grocery store? I flip through my cards! They're always with me! I am in a demanding medical program, and I swear by this app!

reviews.t: Hate whatever they did with this update
reviews.x: I haven’t gone on it since spring , but they’re update is annoying and keeps messing up my notes. It is now an inconvenience

Super useful! The best flashcard app out there, way better than Anki. Actually, it’s the best language learning app other than Memrise, and it’s actually not ONLY a language app. It autofills translations if you create on the phone. My quibbles are mostly about paid features which are sort of half-baked so far. The offline storage is arbitrarily and doesn’t let you specify what you want to keep. I went on vacay with no internet and couldn’t use it. The long-term learning feature needs tweaking too, but it’s not that necessary since it tracks your progress, so you’ll know what needs practicing.I have SO many decks, but navigating them isn't always easy. I'm currently learning Spanish, but all my old Russian decks keep popping up to the top of the list, without me using them, some because the owner updates them, etc. If the sorting were better and the offline decks was really functional, it’d be a 5 star app. But for now, it’s a 5-star website, a 4 star app, and maybe dock a star for the paid version. I really paid just to support the company for doing a good job, but I’m waiting for the kinks to be worked out!

Really easy to use, fantastic layout, and has been a huge help in memorizing medical terminology. I love the auto-fill function. My one issue is that the app doesn't give the option to add folders in classes; if this was added as a feature it would be a HUGE boost to organization, but maybe that's a paid perk (I'm using the free version).

I had information that the activities there were free, after install there were the options free or paid, I chose Free mode, but it didn't work, simply it freezes in an update screen, so I should upgrade before any activity. Uninstalling now. If you want to pay, I had excellent references of this app. For me it's not interesting.

The app itself is clean and modern looking. It is very helpful and easy to use however there are things to improve. One of those is for example writting mathematical fractions, there is no way to do it except writting them in plain text with slashes which to me looks very ugly. Second thing is the viewing of created sets from pc on smartphones. On pc everything seems to work fine for instance bold text, different color selections of text and the images but on smartphone images are way too small.

Not bad: has import/export, handles multiple possible answers (but only on one side of the card). But I can't get past the fact that learning progress is reset when the app deems the card set to be "learned". It's very awkward to use this app as I need to add more cards every few days. This app is not able to keep continuous track of which cards I'm comfortable with and which are new.

This app is as good as it gets for studying foreign language words. Much more fun and manageable than cardstock. *You can't break big decks down into little decks, so you always have to make little decks if you don't study a lot at once. You also can't combine them through the app, so that context often gives away your vocabulary words. *It should really have its own IME: I type my target language almost exclusively on Quizlet so my study words are always auto-suggested when I'm studying them.

Overall a great app. The interface is really easy to use and I found it extremely helpful when studying(especially languages). There are all kinds of quizes you can find and if needed, you can make your own. The good thing is that the app can quiz you on the material in many different ways so you really remember what you learn. 100% would recommend .

Super Helpful. I've been using this app for 4 years now and it makes studying so much easier. I can access and edit my flash cards from any device. My friends can access them too and use them just the same. You can put passwords on your sets so only certain people can edit or even see them. The free version has worked just fine for me so far but if you want to do voice recordings and use your own pictures, then you would have to pay.

Excellent, very highly recommended! I used mine to build my own revision card sets for a high level Health and Safety exam and extensively used it to help pass all 3 with great marks. The more effort you put it to build good sets, the more it pays off. The fact that my sets are now available for others to use (as I can use others) is super.

I've found this app brilliant BUT PLEASE DEVELOPERS!! could you limit the number of terms that you can become 'familiar' with when learning? when there's a large set it gets impossible to learn when the number of terms you're looking at keeps increasing! it's really off putting and I've had to split up sets into smaller groups to stop this happening. perhaps this could be an adjustable feature? THANK YOU!

I use quizlet for EVERY test. You can study anywhere, anytime (even when driving to school 😊). Plus, you don't have to constantly carry a big stack of flashcards around and freak out when you think you've lost one. The best part is that you can add pictures to the cards, which is incredibly helpful for classes where you need to ID certain things (i.e., igneous vs. metamorphic vs. sedimentary rock, or plant ID). I don't usually make them on my phone though, since typing is easier on a computer.

I really love the overall simplicity of the application. i just wish that the testing format would allow for a little more room for error. For example I would sometimes use plural wording in my notecards and that would cause me to get a question wrong. Even with this issue though the app allows for you to select when you got a question right despite minor spelling errors so it is a very minor issue.

I like the app. I do think it needs some sort of tracker that follows how many times you get a card right or wrong. Then have a graph where you can chart sets, classes, and certain cards. I was looking at some of the other flash card apps, this is the only one that will read the words on the card to you. (although, being able to slow down the speed it reads at would be nice.)

Great App, helps me study for multiple subjects like science, mandarin, ELA, etc. I'm glad I can change the way I answer, like multiple choice, written, etc but I do wish there was an option where I can put different answers on one question and only one is right. but this app still deserves 5 stars, plus I only get ads that are on the side, so I can continue studying and there are hardly any ads

Quizlet is amazing! It allows me to learn subjects at my pace without the gigantic cost of text books. I only wish that it had Canadian version. Often my answers are correct, but because of the Canadian spelling, they are flagged as incorrect. Also, the US Social Work study contains content on US laws and services that do not exist in Canada and are therefore irrelevant. Is there a CDN version in the works? Other than that, it is great!

Quizlet is a superb study tool that I can always rely on to help me memorize vocabulary terms! I would definitely suggest this to anyone feels like physical flashcards aren't helping enough, since this contains multiple types of study tools, like flashcards, multiple choice questions, true and false questions, writing and practice tests. It also provides notifications to remind you to study for a test.

Quizlet has been very helpful with my studies (medical billing/coding) and didn't realize there were so many selections of subjects. I always thought it was just for young kids. I like how there are different styles of studying and practice tests/games too. I highly recommend this app if you need a little extra help.

Extremely customizable! It's nearly the perfect digitization of vocabulary studying. The only thing that could make quizlet better, in my opinion, is to expand the number of vocab words that appear in any one "matching" game. But that might be a matter of screen size. If you are learning a new language, need to master a restaurant menu, or taking vocab-heavy courses, I think you should buy the quizlet premium membership. It is totally worth unlimited vocab studying sessions!

I upgraded to the Plus because it said I could use pictures. I spent a couple hours making sets with a picture for the answer. I can see the front and back UNTIL I tap on flashcards, then NOTHING, just 3 dots where the picture should be. I thought maybe it took a few hours to upload, it's been 3 days. I've spent 3 days trying to look on line for help & under quizlet. I've emailed twice with no response. Has anyone else had this issue? If so, any advice would sure be appreciated! Thank you

I am very pleased with the app and made progress with studying for upcoming tests but I wish it would be more useful when it come to studying for other subjects than language. It would be nice if we could add a third section to the cards so that we could write the word, the explanation and then an example.

It's a great app to study from. However, the "go" features very rarely function - a total of one of my sets out of God knows how many I need to learn has actually downloaded fully. It's been a couple of days since I've upgraded and I've been online for most of that. Oh, and the free trial? Doesn't actually give you a free trial. Basically, I've paid £9.99 for night theme. Please add an option to select which sets to download.

I love this app because it is a fun, mobile way to study. I've always loved to make flashcards for math formulas, vocabulary words, and short answers. This app makes it quick and easy to make flashcards, shuffle them, and test myself in a variety of ways. It is also very nice that I can study anywhere I have my phone!

I've found Quizlet very useful for revising terms and definitions for lots of subjects, escpecially for vocabulary and quotations, but some things mean it's not the best it could be. I would like it if I could: edit individual terms and merge sets and import lists on the app; turn off auto capitalisation and change my username more than once! Also could we choose which sets to download, and maybe not have to pay to download a small number of sets, like 4 or 5, or a certain number or terms, 800?

It is an ok app. Not as good as Anki for studying. Edit: after using for a long time: I took a star away because in Quizlet it is too hard to organize your cards once you have a lot of them. If you plan on adding a lot of study material I suggest searching for another app. The search in the app is bad. I just searched for cards in one of my classes and they don't show up. I can find them easily on the web with the same search terms. I have contacted customer support about all these issues and the response is that they don't plan on making any changes.

I like quizlet. It is soooooooooooooooooooo easy to use! Pro's Very helpful if you haven't studied for a while, and your test is this week. Con's I dislike it when you search for something, and the first thing that pops up are your own study sets. Then you have to scroll down a while to find your searched set. Con's Some study sets are inaccurate! Pro's It is very easy to make your own accurate study sets. Con's I just wish the NIGHT THEME will be free one of these days. People need it!

Very useful and helps me pass tests. One of many various problems is that it detects words inputted that weren't plural/were plural as wrong. For example, the answer is samples, but you put sample, and recognizes it as wrong. Sometimessupposed to be specific, but COME ON! This is just infuriating, and makes me want to break my phone. Please fix this and I'll at least give you 4 stars. 😡

Great additional study resource. Convenient way to keep flashcards with you at all times for a quick study when you have downtime. And sometimes the hard work has been done for you because you can use other people's flashcards if they're available for your class. Saved a lot of time not making flaahcards. Thanks to those who have made flashcards public for others.

It's very useful, but I really, really wish you could check off words that you know and don't want to pop up anymore. You can favorite certain terms, but often that's a much more cumbersome way to go about things because you have to reassess them constantly, whereas if you could check off words as you're sure you've got them, it'd be infinitely more convenient.

this is a great tool for studying any subject. there is ads but they are so small they don't at all interfere and most of the time you don't notice them, so I see no reason for taking off stars for something that isn't even a problem. it works with almost every subject from first responder to English vocab. if you are looking for a great free study tool look no further.

Great tool to help study for quizzes and exams. The plus version is so WORTH the money. Having access to photos and audio samples in your study sets makes studying faster and more efficient. There are so many more sets available on the plus version. Since upgrading, I have been able to find an existing set for most of my terms. The time I save is worth the 12.00 for a year. I highly recommend the upgrade if you find yourself spending a lot of time creating sets. happy studying ! 😊

Quizlet is a great and useful app. 🔶 However there is one important missing feature: it would be great to track wrong answered terms not only in the tests but in the set itself. Saying so, there might be a seperate section (just like 'learn', 'test' and more) containing ferequently missed terms. Or it can be a simple sorting feature in set cards itself just like 'Original order' and 'Alphabetical'.

I've been using Quizlet for 3 years now. It's a great way to quickly learn terminologies and stuff that are hard to memorize if you will just simply read it again and again. I love it! But the thing is I want the old Quizlet back. The one that lets you view your flashcards offline and lets you upload images for free because it was like that before. That's my only complain that's why I'm giving 3 stars only. I hope you make those features free again.

There are some terrible 'teachers' on this app and by that I mean some lessons are inaccurate or poorly structured but wading through them you will find some gems! You can add the best ones you find to folders you can create so you can find them easily. I've been using it for music theory, piano and guitar and have found the app very useful indeed for learning when it's too late to practice.

The best app of its kind! You can write cards yourself or get already existing sets of words. It's easy and useful for learning any language! Besides cards it has other options of learning words. Like the exercise where you have to match a picture to the right word as fast as you can and etc.

I use it for Japanese, it's actually very useful. the predictive flash card creation is helpful for making sets of cards. organisation is better than other flash cards apps I've used previously. in combination with paper or another device to write on, one of the best ways to learn vocabulary or other writing systems like the kanji in Japanese.

Great app for any level of school. Makes it so much easier to learn vocabulary. I used to procrastinate to make my flash cards because all of the writing. Makes it so much easier. They even give you suggestions for the definition so you can even type less. Love it! Got so many A's from using it.

Absolutely love it! I'm constantly learning languages, and this app is the best. I've tried other flash-cards apps but this one is liiit. So easy to use, doesn't require much effort to create sets. I stick to the free version because there's no reason for me to purchase extended subscription. Also, there aren't annoying ads that pop up every second. I use both the website when using a laptop or a desktop and the mobile app. Both are brilliant!

I love this app. It has really helped me learn new languages, and expand my borders. You can learn anything on Quizlet. There is only one thing that you can improve on; there should be more new modes that could come out each month, and also perhaps themes for Christmas and Halloween ect. Thank you, Quizlet, for helping me grow, and for teaching me so much.

Like the online client the app works well. There isn't much to say about the functionality. The problem I have is with the stupid subscription pricing. The small added benefits do not nessesitate a subscription model no matter how small. It's just a cash grab. It should be a one time fee of 5 bucks or less. Give me a break, 2 bucks a month for night mode and offline use.

I love how I can access it from anywhere but I would appreciate it more if there was more variety and suggestive content that help you study for a particular subject. For example it is more difficult to use this info for listing characteristic feature like biology as opposed to learning a language which is straight definitional and only usually only have one meaning. It is also difficult to use gor mathematical sciences like chemistry which require exponents and subscripts to convey information.

The only reason I am not giving it five stars is that the app needs better text to speech conversion. I use it for language learning, and the Dutch text to speech is terrible. It would be nice if you could also control the pronunciation speed. Memrise is miles ahead of quizlet is this regard. Overall though, I find quizlet extremely useful and efficient at "brute force" memorization.

I love Quizlet, so the app makes me happy. It would be nice to be able to add cards directly at whatever point in the card sequence I choose vs. scrolling to the bottom. It would make it more convenient for keeping groups organized together within a large stack of cards. For example, being able to have one lesson of cards successfully grouped together within an entire unit of cards vs. new additions needing to be dragged all the way from the bottom of a large stack.

fantastic practice tool. access to other user sets is a huge time saver. just need to make sure to double check accuracy of others' answers. also, the games one can create from the flashcards are very helpful. if using the app's automatic game creation, flashcards don't always translate well into the template game structure. otherwise, I love it.

Absolutely AMAZING!!!!!!!!!!!!!! This app makes studying at home so much more fun and "easier" with my 8 year old. She loves her phone, and since using this app, she ENJOYS her "screen time" (as I call it at home) and all while I, Mommy, enjoys it as well. She is learning, studying, yet also is on her phone helping the studying process be a lot more exciting than sitting at the kitchen table with paper and a pencil, all while she is loosing interest. ABSOLUTELY 100 PERCENT GRATEFUL FOR SUCH A PRODUCT THAT ACTUALLY HELPS MAKE LEARNING THAT MUCH EASIER AND LESS STRESSFUL!! NOT to mention less fighting or arguing when it comes to homework time. Also. This app can be used in the car, waiting in line at the grocery store, doctor appointments, etc. Definitely 100 percent worth 5 stars!!!!!

Brilliant app. One of the most useful on my phone. But is there is anyway of hiding the sets. By that I mean when you open the app, you see your sets and then your folders when you scroll down. But Is there a way by which I can hide all my sets and just see my sets within my folders. Mainly for organisation purposes only. However brilliant app. So much value added to peoples lives using this app.

The app has a lot of good features for creating, using, and sharing sets of flashcards. Unfortunately, it is really impractical to manage large sets of cards. You can't search or tag or sort or split or merge or... Anything, really. I would use the app a lot more if I could maintain and update sets over a longer period of time.

Great app, easy to create quizzes and easy to use, the app is perfect for revision, would easily recommend Edit: on mobile, some keyboards do not have the ability to type accents, a way of typing them by using the app would be great, as I am kept being told my answers are wrong even though I know the answer, I am just unable to write the accent in. Edit 2: I managed to find out how to add accents, but I have recently discovered another problem, if you use learn on mobile quizlet at some point learn on that particular quiz will no longer work on laptop. Thank you for reading.

Great! I use it to study and revise Chinese and I simply love it. Not only does it have flashcards, but also a lot of functions to actively learn the words (ex. Listening, writing) and games to play to test your vocabulary! There are no ads and all the basic functions, that are definetly enough to study, are included in the free version. I couldn't have asked for a better tool. Thanks Quizlet!

I've just recently downloaded the app to learn my Korean lessons and I can already see how great this app can help in my studying. Creating the content is breeze, especially if you're learning a new language. I use the Hangul word for the term and automatically it gives me options for the English equivalent in the description. Doing the flashcards and activities helps cement what I've learned. Only issue is at the part where I need to type in the answer in Hangeul. It gives me a check mark (done) after typing, but clicking on this button automatically brings me to the next question and assumes that where I click is my answer. Other than that, works great!

I really like to use this app to study specifically for medical terminology as it involves A LOT of terms to learn and memorize. My complaint is that it seems as if after you get past or close to around 100 terms, it becomes VERY laggy. It takes at least 10 seconds to go from one definition to the next term when typing them in. This causes a lot of frustration because the time that I have to wait for the cursor to go to the next thing adds up. All of my chapters have well over 100 terms each so this is something I have to deal with every single time I have a new chapter. I'm sure this wouldn't happen if I purchase the premium version, but I'm a broke college student that's just trying to study.

I love this App! It allows me to enter my own data, access it quickly, and test myself on the things I need to know for the week. I especially love that I can literally make files, and store everything class related from Terms to remember, to my practice test and answers. Later when I take my certification exams, I'll he able to study the whole course from start to finish. I also like that you can look up others and see there input.

reviews.t: Does not run on an IPod 5 iOS 9.3.5
reviews.x: I love using quizlet online but when I downloaded it on my iPod 5, it will not open. It stays on the opening page and then seems to crash and sends me back to my homescreen. Had to delete it. (I am running iOS 9.3.5 which is supposed to be compatible with the app)

reviews.t: My whole program is in flash cards now!!
reviews.x: This app has revolutionized my studying habits! Me and my roommates all take turns converting the days lecture power points into flash cards. We now have 3 full semesters of cards for every class, and they are all accessible no matter where we are! I believe that the process of making questions out of lecture content and reviewing the cards is one of the most effective ways to study. I would also recommend upgrading to the plus version solely for the ability to add your own pictures from lectures/classes
Great to study
